definitions.explanation: Cooking oil used specifically for deep-frying foods such as tempura, tonkatsu, and croquettes.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}を{温|あたた}める。
{揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}の{温度|おんど}は{百八十度|ひゃくはちじゅうど}がいい。
examples.english: The frying oil should be at 180 degrees.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}い{終|お}わった{揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}は、{固|かた}めて{燃|も}えるゴミとして{捨|す}てる。
examples.english: Used frying oil should be solidified and disposed of as combustible waste.

notes:
Compound of {揚|あ}げる (to deep-fry) + {油|あぶら} (oil). Refers specifically to oil used for deep-frying, as opposed to cooking oil in general.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}を{熱|ねっ}する: to heat frying oil
- {揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}の{温度|おんど}: frying oil temperature
- {揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}を{処理|しょり}する: to dispose of frying oil
- {揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}を{替|か}える: to change the frying oil

RELATED WORDS:
- サラダ{油|あぶら}: salad oil, vegetable oil — the most common type of oil used for frying in Japanese kitchens
- {天|てん}ぷら{油|あぶら}: tempura oil — often used interchangeably with {揚|あ}げ{油|あぶら}
- {廃油|はいゆ}: waste oil — used frying oil that needs to be disposed of

COOKING NOTE:
Proper frying oil temperature is important in Japanese cooking: around 160°C for low-temperature frying, 170-180°C for standard frying ({天|てん}ぷら, {唐揚|からあ}げ), and 180-190°C for high-temperature frying.
